_comment: Byte-exact encode/decode pairs for the Pico->ESP SAFETY_CMD_POWER (0x0E) payload, per docs/LINK_PROTOCOL.md sec 6, Frame E -- the 55-byte layout (KILNLINK_POWER_LEN). payload_hex is the raw command payload as it would sit inside kilnlink_frame_t.payload -- see frame_vectors.json for the outer envelope. Generated by hand-computing struct.pack('<f'/'<d') in Python and cross-checked against kilnlink_power_encode/decode in test/test_power.c.

vectors.name: healthy_reading
vectors.note: flags = MAINS_VOLTAGE_CONFIGURED|CALIBRATED (0x05), 240V mains, two conducting channels with distinct current/duty/power, third channel idle (all zero, not NaN -- idle is a legitimate zero, only invalidity is NaN).

vectors.name: mains_not_configured
vectors.note: MAINS_VOLTAGE_CONFIGURED clear -- LINK_PROTOCOL.md sec 6 Frame E: mains_voltage_v is NaN when not set, and every p_avg_w/p_total_w that depends on it is NaN too, even though the channel currents/fractions themselves are still real readings.

vectors.name: channel_clipped
vectors.note: flags = MAINS_VOLTAGE_CONFIGURED|ANY_CHANNEL_CLIPPED (0x03). Channel 0 clipped -- its own p_avg_w is NaN despite mains_voltage_v being configured, and p_total_w is NaN too since it has an invalid contributor. Channels 1/2 are idle zero, not NaN.

hostile_vectors.name: too_short
hostile_vectors.note: 54 bytes -- one short of the fixed 55-byte frame. This frame has no length field of its own to lie about; the wire length itself is the only signal, so a decoder must reject anything that isn't exactly 55 bytes.

hostile_vectors.name: too_long
hostile_vectors.note: 56 bytes -- one more than the fixed 55-byte frame. Equally invalid; this is a fixed-size frame, not a minimum size.

hostile_vectors.name: wrong_cmd
hostile_vectors.note: Byte 0 is 0x01 (GET_STATUS's id), not 0x0E -- an otherwise well-formed 55-byte buffer whose command byte says it's a different frame.
